THIS IS A RE-CUT. The original branch/PR for this deliverable (#57, branch lwb-confirm-hook-fires) carried the identical evidence and content, but its first commit's diff added a literal POSIX home-directory checkout path (this container's, in an early draft of the new doc) -- caught locally by python -m pytest tests/ -q / tests/test_lwb_check_env_leak.py, and independently by CI's lwb-env-leak --range step -- before a later commit on that branch fixed the file's final content. scripts/lwb_check_env_leak.py --range scans the ADDED lines of every commit in a range by design (its own docstring: a leak that one commit added and a later commit in the same range removed still fails), so the fix-in-place could never clear that check, and force-push is denied in this environment, so the introducing commit could not be corrected. This branch re-cuts from scratch: the doc was written correctly (with the placeholder token this repo's sanitiser convention uses for a checkout path) in its very first commit here, so the leak was never introduced into this branch's history at all -- verified below. The PR is now open as #58; "pr": 58 was added in a follow-up commit per proof/README.md's PR-authority rule.

THE LIVE CLAUDE CODE SESSIONS THEMSELVES (the actual evidence for item 1.8) are not re-run as commands[] entries in this record -- each costs real Anthropic API usage, is not byte-for-byte reproducible (fresh session_id, timestamps, model routing), and running them again here would not change what already happened. Their exact commands, full transcripts' relevant fields, and the ledger files they produced are captured verbatim in docs/maintainers/hook-fires-verification-2026-09-24.md; the two `cat .../ledger-*.jsonl` commands[] entries above reproduce the ledger evidence that record quotes, byte for byte, with sha256 digests of their own.

OS/VERSION COVERAGE: every command above, and both live Claude Code sessions, ran on one Linux container (Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Python 3.11.15, Claude Code 2.1.282) only. Windows and macOS were not exercised for the live-session evidence; scripts/lwb_check_hook_launch.py (launch-mechanics only, not a live session) is the only piece of this that CI runs cross-platform.

PERMISSION MODE: only --permission-mode dontAsk (with a --settings allow-list for Bash/Task) was exercised end-to-end. --dangerously-skip-permissions and --permission-mode bypassPermissions were tried first and refused outright by the CLI in this root-privileged container ("cannot be used with root/sudo privileges"), so they were never observed either firing or not firing the hook. Other permission modes were not tried.

POLICY CONTENT: the bundled default policy's only rule, lwb_version, always allows and only ever warns -- this record and the new doc establish that the hook FIRES and is OBSERVED, not that deny-mode policy behavior works correctly inside a live session (that is a separate, untested question).
